purpose: Represent people only through independently typed, evidence-scoped relationships to exact artifacts, concepts, practices, implementations, and compiler/library decisions.
constitutional_laws: LLM or generative contribution != core corpus eligibility

node_kinds.person_candidate: A human identity candidate with explicit disambiguation state.
node_kinds.artifact_work: An intellectual or technical work independent of any one manifestation.
node_kinds.artifact_edition: A content-addressed or version-pinned manifestation; DOI registration without a digest is explicitly only an edition candidate.
node_kinds.contribution_assertion: A qualified person-artifact relationship with role, evidence scope, claim state, and limitations.
node_kinds.concept: A governed analytical or data-system concept learned from content review.
node_kinds.family: A non-collapsible contribution family used for coverage, never a fame category.
node_kinds.implementation: A versioned executable realization distinct from method or artifact.
node_kinds.replication: Independent reproduction, benchmark, critique, or falsification of a claim.
node_kinds.compiler_mapping: A candidate mapping from a learned contract to compiler IR, proof, decision, library, product, or target qualification.
node_kinds.review_item: An unresolved identity, role, content, precedence, limitation, or mapping question.
node_kinds.evidence_source: A locator plus the exact facts it is authoritative enough to support.

contribution_roles.conceptualized: CRediT-like conceptualization, admitted only from explicit contribution evidence.
contribution_roles.implemented_software: Software contribution explicitly evidenced by project records.
contribution_roles.curated_data: Data or benchmark curation explicitly evidenced.
contribution_roles.maintains: Current or historical maintenance role; not original invention.
contribution_roles.advocated: Public advocacy or teaching; not evidence of implementation.

admission_rules: A person may enter as a candidate from a search seed, but expertise is not admitted until exact identity and relevant artifacts are reviewed.
Bibliographic metadata may admit authored edges only; it cannot admit invented, conceptualized, maintained, or independently replicated edges.
Every artifact claim carries an evidence scope and at least one limitation.
Every compiler/library mapping remains candidate until content review identifies the precise semantic contract and an executable test or proof obligation.
LLM/generative-only artifacts are excluded; mixed portfolios retain independently relevant non-LLM artifacts.
Same-name, missing-identifier, title-only, affiliation-only, and ambiguous contribution cases enter review queues instead of being silently resolved.

A DOI identifies a registered work/manifestation relationship but does not by itself pin bytes, edition semantics, corrections, or retractions; content digest or version evidence is required for an executable edition.

source_alignment.use: Agent/entity/activity and qualified attribution, association, delegation, role, derivation, and invalidation distinctions.
Contributor-role vocabulary that complements undifferentiated authorship.
Persistent identifiers, creator/contributor distinctions, related identifiers, resource types, dates, and versioning.
Computer-science bibliographic discovery and author identifiers only.
Cross-domain bibliographic discovery and identity candidates only.
